title: Teacher-written model postcard from the Grand Canyon
subject: English
source: Written for english/y4 lesson 84 (Teacher-written model postcard from the Grand Canyon (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 84: Reading postcards: informal, first person, present tense. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Teacher-written model postcard for TGA
paras: We're at the Grand Canyon! It's huge: the rocks are striped red, orange and gold, and the river looks like a silver thread far below. We're staying near the edge, and tonight we'll watch the stars. I can't wait to show you my photos.

head: Feature
Example
rows: It's huge; the rocks are striped

panels.title: Why short?
points: Room for the address and stamp

keywords.def: a card with a picture of a place and a short message
friendly, chatty language for people we know

questions.q: Find a simile in the postcard
What tense is 'the rocks are striped'?
Core: label six features on the model postcard
Extend: change three sentences from the postcard into formal language
questions.a: For example: We are at the Grand Canyon. It is very large.

questions.q: Stretch: explain why the writer uses the present tense
questions.a: Because the postcard is written during the trip, about what is happening now

options: I am writing to inform you of our visit.
questions.a: C) We're having an amazing time!. We're is a contraction and amazing is chatty; the others are formal.
